subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y10 lesson 57 (Own 4GE1-style exam questions with indicative mark points (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 57: Coastal transport, longshore drift and deposition (2.1b). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Draw an annotated longshore drift diagram, then answer: (a) State two sources of coastal sediment. (2) (b) Explain why deposition occurs in bays. (3)
questions.a: (a) rivers, cliff erosion, offshore bars (b) waves refract and spread out in bays, losing energy, so sediment is dropped
questions.model: Teacher draws the first two zig-zags with arrows.

questions.q: Suggest how to measure longshore drift on a beach (fieldwork design).
questions.a: Place a marked float or painted pebble; measure distance moved in a set time with a tape; repeat; record wind direction

questions.q: Explain the idea of a sediment cell.
questions.a: A stretch of coast where sediment circulates; inputs, transfers and stores; actions in one place affect others in the cell

questions.q: Why do groynes cause erosion further along the coast?
questions.a: They trap sediment on the updrift side (1), so less reaches downdrift beaches, which get narrower and erode (1)
questions.model: Groyne traps sand. Sand cannot pass. Beach downdrift starves. Erosion increases there.
